short: Theodosius I's win over a Western usurper briefly reunited the empire under one ruler for the last time.
full:
The Western emperor Valentinian II died in 392 in disputed circumstances, and the general Arbogast installed the pagan-leaning senator Eugenius as a puppet emperor in the West. Theodosius I, ruling in the East and a committed Christian, marched against them, meeting Eugenius's and Arbogast's forces on 5 and 6 September 394 along the Frigidus River (the modern Vipava) in present-day Slovenia.

The first day went badly for Theodosius, but a violent local wind, the bora, reportedly turned in his favour on the second day, and defections from Eugenius's ranks decided the battle. Eugenius was killed and Arbogast took his own life days later. Theodosius briefly ruled the reunited empire alone before his death the following January, after which he divided it permanently between his sons Arcadius and Honorius, a split the Western and Eastern empires never again reversed.
